meaning:
Many online scams are often associated with the Advance-fee scam. This scam and other types of fraud are often referred to as “419”. The number “419” refers to the section of the Nigerian Criminal Code dealing with fraud, the charges and penalties for offenders.

African Nations such as Nigeria, Togo, Ivory Coast and South Africa are often known for the origins of many fraudulent scams.

line: You won’t catch me with no dead CC (Okay)
vault_lines: You won't catch me with no dead CC (Okay)
meaning:
CC is an abbreviation for Credit Card . G4choppa explains that won’t catch him with a Credit Card that’s not working.

A “CC” can also refer to a carbon copy. A scammer may make an exact copy of a bank card. G4choppa saying that the copy will not be “dead”, means that it will high quality and it will not be easily traced or investigated by police.

line: I got the wave, no durag (Mmh)
vault_lines: I got the wave, no durag (Mmh)
meaning:
A durag is a scarf typically worn to accelerate the development of waves, braids or dreadlocks in the hair. It helps to keep the moisture of the hair needed for the development of these hair textures.



Without a durag, it is very hard to train hair to the wave hairstyle. Ice Baby is saying that his waves are good enough that he can go around without a durag on or be referencing that he has started a trend (a “wave”) and now others follow.

line: Across social media, particularly on Instagram and Snapchat, temptation is everywhere (Ayy, I swear Fermz and Renz patterned this) Glamorous looking accounts offering get-rich-quick schemes It’s easy money, it almost sounds too good to be true
vault_lines: Glamorous looking accounts offering get-rich-quick schemes
meaning:
The intro comes from a Sky News Report
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WLGX4jQvARI

It explains how fraudsters scam unknowing people who are often desperate for money. The report mainly refers to “Money Mules”, where money from the proceeds of crime are passed through/transferred through a victim’s bank account with the owner of the victim think that they will get a cut of the laundered money. The fraudsters will tell the victim that they need complete control of the account in order to add and remove the illegal money when they need it to be passed through.

Sometimes the owner will get a cut, but more often than not the owner will lose control of their account, all of their funds and may be blacklisted.
